title: Explicit partial contraction for ordered join chains
statement:
Let $r\geq1$ and let $X_0,\ldots,X_{r-1}$ be sets with specified elements $v_i\in X_i$. Let $J_{-1}=\mathbf Z[\varnothing]\cong\mathbf Z$, let $J_q$ for $0\leq q<r$ be the abelian group of finite formal integer sums of symbols $[(i_0,x_0),\ldots,(i_q,x_q)]$ with $0\leq i_0<\cdots<i_q<r$ and $x_j\in X_{i_j}$, and put $J_q=0$ otherwise. The indicated symbol families are specified $\mathbf Z$-bases in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Define $d$ by alternating deletion of vertices, including $d[(i,x)]=[\varnothing]$ and $d[\varnothing]=0$. Define the degree-one homomorphism $c_i$ to be zero on symbols containing color $i$; on a symbol missing color $i$, insert $(i,v_i)$ in its increasing-color position $k$ with coefficient $(-1)^k$. In particular $c_i[\varnothing]=[(i,v_i)]$. Define $R_i$ on symbols missing color $i$ to be zero, and on a symbol containing color $i$ to be that symbol minus the symbol obtained by replacing its color-$i$ vertex by $(i,v_i)$. Put
$$S=\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}(R_0\circ\cdots\circ R_{i-1})\circ c_i,$$
where the empty composite is the identity and the rightmost map is applied first. Then $d^2=0$ and
$$dS_q+S_{q-1}d=\mathrm{id}_{J_q}\qquad(-1\leq q\leq r-2),$$
with $S_{-2}=0$. For every family of maps $u_i:X_i\to Y_i$, with chosen elements $w_i=u_i(v_i)$ in $Y_i$, the induced homomorphisms $J_q(u)$, defined by applying $u_i$ to vertices, satisfy $J_{q+1}(u)S_q^v=S_q^wJ_q(u)$. The displayed formula for $S$ expands on each basis symbol into a finite integer sum of basis symbols obtained only by inserting chosen vertices or replacing vertices by chosen vertices; the coefficient list and the choices of insertions and replacements depend only on $r$ and the list of colors, not on any equality tests among the $x_j$ and $v_i$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion below local continuous-cocycle descent: explicit ordered-join chain calculation; not asserted in the blueprint itself.

proof.text: All maps are defined first on the specified bases, then extended by finite integer linear combination. This gives well-defined homomorphisms: for $d$ there are $q+1$ terms, for $c_i$ at most one, and for $R_i$ at most two. By [def-weil-pbc-free-module], uniqueness of the finite basis expansion shows that two such homomorphisms agree once they agree on every basis symbol. Hence the following calculations on symbols prove identities on the groups; all maps on zero groups are zero.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written ordered-join expansion below local continuous-cocycle descent, calculation 1; not a claim made by the blueprint.

proof.text: Write $\sigma=[z_0,\ldots,z_q]$ and let $D_a\sigma$ denote deletion of position $a$, numbered from zero. For $a<b$, the term deleting original positions $a,b$ occurs in $d^2\sigma$ with coefficients $(-1)^{a+b-1}$ (delete $a$, then position $b-1$) and $(-1)^{a+b}$ (delete $b$, then position $a$). These sum to zero, and every term belongs to exactly one such pair. This also covers $q=1$, where both final symbols are $[\varnothing]$. For $q=0,-1$ the second boundary is zero by definition. Thus $d^2=0$ in all degrees.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written ordered-join expansion below local continuous-cocycle descent, calculation 2; not a claim made by the blueprint.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and suppose $\sigma$ misses color $i$; let $k$ be the number of its colors less than $i$. In $dc_i\sigma$, deletion of the inserted vertex has coefficient $(-1)^k(-1)^k=1$ and gives $\sigma$. For an original vertex in position $a<k$, its deletion has coefficient $(-1)^{k+a}$, whereas its term in $c_id\sigma$ has coefficient $(-1)^{a+k-1}$. For $a\geq k$ these coefficients are respectively $(-1)^{k+a+1}$ and $(-1)^{a+k}$. Each pair cancels, so $(dc_i+c_id)\sigma=\sigma=(1-R_i)\sigma$. For $\sigma=[\varnothing]$ this calculation reads $dc_i[\varnothing]=d[(i,v_i)]=[\varnothing]$, with $c_id[\varnothing]=0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written ordered-join expansion below local continuous-cocycle descent, calculation 3; not a claim made by the blueprint.

proof.text: If instead $\sigma$ contains color $i$ in position $k$, then $c_i\sigma=0$. Among the faces of $\sigma$, only $D_k\sigma$ misses color $i$, so $c_id\sigma=(-1)^k(-1)^kT_i\sigma=T_i\sigma$, where $T_i\sigma$ is obtained by replacing that vertex by $(i,v_i)$. Since $R_i\sigma=\sigma-T_i\sigma$, again $dc_i+c_id=1-R_i$. Together with the preceding step this identity holds on every nonzero degree, including the top degree (there every symbol contains $i$ and $c_i=0$); on the remaining zero groups it holds trivially. No equality between the original vertex and the chosen vertex was assumed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written ordered-join expansion below local continuous-cocycle descent, calculation 4; not a claim made by the blueprint.

proof.text:
Multiplying $R_i=1-dc_i-c_id$ on the left and right by $d$, and using $d^2=0$, gives $dR_i=d-dc_id=R_id$. Set $P_0=1$ and $P_i=R_0\circ\cdots\circ R_{i-1}$ for $1\leq i\leq r$. Each $P_i$ commutes with $d$ by repeated substitution of $dR_j=R_jd$. Hence the stated sum $S=\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}P_ic_i$ satisfies
$$dS+Sd=\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}P_i(dc_i+c_id)=\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}(P_i-P_{i+1})=1-P_r.$$
The middle equality uses $P_iR_i=P_{i+1}$ with precisely the composition order in the statement, and requires no permutation of the factors.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written ordered-join expansion below local continuous-cocycle descent, calculation 5; not a claim made by the blueprint.

proof.text: On a symbol of degree $-1\leq q\leq r-2$, at least one of the $r$ colors, say $j$, is missing. Every $R_i$ either kills a symbol or produces a difference of symbols with the same color list. Thus, when $P_r=R_0\circ\cdots\circ R_{r-1}$ is applied from right to left, every term reaching $R_j$ still misses $j$, and $R_j$ kills it. Therefore $P_r=0$ in the specified degrees, and the preceding identity gives $dS_q+S_{q-1}d=1$. In degree $-1$ only $i=0$ contributes to $S[\varnothing]$: for $i>0$, the factor $R_0$ kills $c_i[\varnothing]$. Consequently $S_{-1}[\varnothing]=[(0,v_0)]$ and $dS_{-1}=1$, consistently with $S_{-2}=0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written ordered-join expansion below local continuous-cocycle descent, calculation 6; not a claim made by the blueprint.

proof.text: For a family $u_i:X_i\to Y_i$ with $u_i(v_i)=w_i$, applying $u$ to a symbol preserves its color list and hence every insertion position. If color $i$ is absent, $J(u)c_i^v\sigma$ and $c_i^wJ(u)\sigma$ are the identical signed symbol with inserted vertex $(i,w_i)$; if present both are zero. If color $i$ is present, both $J(u)R_i^v\sigma$ and $R_i^wJ(u)\sigma$ equal $J(u)\sigma-T_i^wJ(u)\sigma$; if absent both are zero. Thus $J(u)c_i^v=c_i^wJ(u)$ and $J(u)R_i^v=R_i^wJ(u)$ on the bases, including the empty symbol. Composing these equalities in the specified order and summing over $i$ proves $J_{q+1}(u)S_q^v=S_q^wJ_q(u)$. Injectivity of $u_i$ is unnecessary, since the calculation permits cancellation of coincident output symbols.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written ordered-join expansion below local continuous-cocycle descent, calculation 7; not a claim made by the blueprint.

proof.text:
For completeness an unreduced expansion gives the coefficient-list assertion explicitly. Let $C$ be the colors of $\sigma$. The $i$-th summand $P_ic_i\sigma$ is zero if $i\in C$. It is also zero if some $j<i$ is missing from $C$: after inserting color $i$, every preceding replacement preserves the color list, and $R_j$ kills every term. Otherwise let $k=\#\{j\in C:j<i\}$ and, for $A\subseteq\{0,\ldots,i-1\}$, let $\sigma_{i,A}$ be $\sigma$ with $(i,v_i)$ inserted and the vertices of colors in $A$ replaced by their chosen vertices. Distributing the two terms of each $R_j$ gives
$$P_ic_i\sigma=\sum_{A\subseteq\{0,\ldots,i-1\}}(-1)^{k+|A|}\sigma_{i,A}.$$
Indeed each subset records exactly the factors in which the negative replacement term was selected; replacements at different colors affect different positions and do not change any color. This list has $2^i$ terms, with repetitions and zero cancellation left uncollected. The list of indices, replacement choices and signs depends only on $r,C$. It never tests whether $x_j=v_j$, even when some terms coincide. Summing these lists proves the final assertion.
